xs.$description:
Element size, step xs. Recommended as a min/max constraint — components are fluid — but valid as a fixed width or height where a layer genuinely can't grow. Fixed across brand, theme and viewport.

Used in:
min-width, min-height, max-width or max-height of an element. The smallest step; the next one up is size.sm.

Do not:
Do not use it for distances between or inside components — those are spacing.*, even when the number matches. A constraint that has to allow more room takes size.sm.

minimum.$description:
Smallest hit area any interactive target may have, on every brand, theme and viewport — locked to the WCAG 2.2 AA floor (SC 2.5.8). A target that has to be smaller only passes through the spacing exception: a circle of this size centred on it must not overlap another target.

Used in:
min-width and min-height of any interactive target, and the spacing check between them.

Do not:
Do not use it as the default hit area — a primary touch action takes size.touch-target.recommended; this is the floor, not the target.

recommended.$description:
Comfortable hit area for touch-first use, on every brand, theme and viewport — locked to the platform guidance (Apple HIG, WCAG 2.5.5) because these products are used with fingers even on desktop.

Used in:
min-width and min-height of a primary touch action — the visible shape may be smaller, the hit area may not.

Do not:
Do not force it on a compact control — those keep their own size step and satisfy size.touch-target.minimum through padding or spacing.
